correction.text: Tortosa and its district, occupied by Raymond IV in 1102

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1111 but the infobox gives "Established: 1102" with Tortosa as capital (1102-1109): "Raymond IV occupied Tortosa in 1102 and prepared to take Tripoli in 1103". Tripoli itself held out until 1109.

correction.text: Cliopatria's first shape, taken back to the fall of Tripoli in 1109

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "Tripoli fell on 12 July 1109"; Bertrand became the first count. Cliopatria has no shape until 1111; its first shape (4.2 k km2: Tripoli, Byblos, Batroun, Safita, Akkar) is used for 1109-1110.

4.2 k km2 for 1111-1125 (Tripoli, Batroun, Byblos, the Safita and Akkar hinterland). The page gives no area figure, so no comparison. "Genoese forces received about a quarter of the land seized around Tripoli. Guglielmo Embriaco was awarded Byblos."

6.2 k km2 for 1126-1138, the largest shape: adds the Buqai'ah plain and Montferrand (Ba'rin). Montferrand was lost in 1137 (Battle of Ba'rin: "the permanent loss of the Crusader castle of Montferrand"); the step to the 1139 shape (5.96 k km2) is that loss.

5.96 k km2 for 1139-1187. 1142: Krak des Chevaliers given by Raymond II to the Hospitallers; 1144: "Raymond II gave the Knights Hospitaller large stretches of frontier land along the Buqai'ah plain"; the lands stay inside the county. In 1166 Nur ad-Din "temporarily captured several castles in the County of Tripoli".

3.2 k km2 for 1188-1271, roughly half of the 1139 shape. The page opened for Krak says Saladin led an army toward it in May 1188 but "decided it was too well defended" and marched on Margat, "where he also failed". What the county lost in 1188 is not on the pages opened (unverified: page budget); the ledger records it at confidence 1. The lordship of Byblos (Gibelet) is outside the shape although "Peter of Gibelet kept his lands for about 10 more years" after 1289.

ledger.note: 1102: Raymond IV of Toulouse occupies Tortosa and founds the county. Infobox "Established: 1102"; "Raymond IV occupied Tortosa in 1102 and prepared to take Tripoli in 1103".

region.text: the city of Tripoli and its land

ledger.note: 1109: Tripoli falls on 12 July. "Under a united Christian onslaught, Tripoli fell on 12 July 1109, completing the Kingdom of Jerusalem." Bertrand, backed by Baldwin I and a Genoese fleet, becomes the first count; Genoa received about a quarter of the land and Guglielmo Embriaco was awarded Byblos.
1109: the capital moves from Tortosa to Tripoli. Infobox "Tortosa (1102-1109), Tripoli (1109-1289)".

region.text: the castle of Montferrand (Ba'rin) and its district; approximate site, no gazetteer place

ledger.note: 1137: Zengi wins at Ba'rin and takes Montferrand. "At the Battle of Ba'rin, Zengi defeated Fulk of Jerusalem's force, which led to the permanent loss of the Crusader castle of Montferrand." County of Tripoli page: "In 1137, Raymond II, the reigning count, lost control of Montferrand." The site is approximate (the gazetteer lacks Montferrand); Cliopatria's 1126 and 1139 shapes are identical at cell scale, so no shape difference marks the loss.

region.text: the part of the 1139 shape outside the 1188 shape

ledger.note: 1188: Cliopatria's shape halves (5.96 k to 3.2 k km2) although the pages opened name no loss: in May 1188 Saladin "decided [Krak] was too well defended" and marched on Margat, "where he also failed to take the castle". Bridging step at confidence 1: page silent on the lands and the year.

region.text: Krak des Chevaliers, Chastel Blanc and the county outside Tripoli

ledger.note: 1271: Baibars takes Krak des Chevaliers on 8 April. "the garrison capitulated" on a forged letter "for them to surrender on 8 April 1271" after he "captured the smaller castles in the area, including Chastel Blanc". The region is the 1188 shape minus the 1272 shape (the Buqai'ah plain and the Krak district).
1289: Batroun and Nephin fall "soon" after Tripoli; the page gives no date. Byblos' lord Peter of Gibelet kept his lands for about ten more years as a tributary of the sultan.

1289: Tripoli falls on 26 April. "The Mamluks captured the city on 26 April"; the population was massacred and Tripoli "razed to the ground"; Qalawun had it rebuilt a few miles inland. Infobox "Conquered by Qalawun: 27 April 1289".

union.text: Byblos (Gibelet), the lordship of Peter of Gibelet

region.text: Tripoli with Batroun and Nephin ("captured soon after Tripoli fell") and the lordship of Byblos (Gibelet) held until about 1299

ledger.note: 1289: the County of Tripoli ends with the Mamluk conquest. "The county fell and was merged into his empire on 27 April 1289"; Mongol alliance sought in March 1289 and Lucia fled to Cyprus.

wars.name: Siege of Tripoli (1102-1109)

zones.text: the city of Tripoli and its land

wars.outcome: Raymond IV occupied Tortosa in 1102, began the citadel on Mons Peregrinus and died on 25 February 1105; Bertrand, backed by Baldwin I and a Genoese fleet, took Tripoli on 12 July 1109 and became its first count as Baldwin's vassal.

wars.name: Battle of Ba'rin

zones.text: the castle of Montferrand (Ba'rin) and its district; approximate site, no gazetteer place

wars.outcome: Zengi defeated Fulk of Jerusalem and Raymond II; the castle of Montferrand was permanently lost.

wars.name: Nur ad-Din's raids on the county
wars.outcome: In 1166 Nur ad-Din "temporarily captured several castles in the County of Tripoli"; no lasting change.

wars.name: Saladin's campaign of 1188
wars.outcome: In May 1188 Saladin led an army toward Krak des Chevaliers, judged it "too well defended" and marched on Margat, where he also failed; the lands Cliopatria shows lost in 1188 are not named by the pages.

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of Krak des Chevaliers

zones.text: Krak and the county outside Tripoli

wars.outcome: Baibars' army arrived on 3 March 1271, took Chastel Blanc and smaller castles, and the Krak garrison surrendered on 8 April 1271 on a forged letter.

wars.name: Siege of Tripoli (1289)

zones.text: Tripoli and the last coastal land

wars.outcome: Qalawun besieged Tripoli from March 1289 and took it on 26 April; Batroun and Nephin fell soon after, Byblos paid tribute; the old city was razed.
wars.note: The Genoese commune and Venice had galleys in the harbour; the Ilkhanate "still did not show much interest in protecting Tripoli".

certainty.note: The county was a narrow coastal and hill strip with Hospitaller and Genoese enclaves; the pages give no surveyed boundary.

notes: County of Tripoli. Five pages opened (budget 5). Cliopatria starts in 1111 (the county dates from 1102: two new keyframes for 1102-1108 at Tortosa and 1109-1110) and runs to 1293 (Tripoli fell on 26/27 April 1289). The infobox gives 27 April 1289, the siege page 26 April. Cliopatria's 1272 and 1285 shapes (454 km2, Tripoli alone) omit Batroun, Nephin and the lordship of Byblos that the siege page shows still in Christian hands in 1289; the correction adds them (confidence 2; the years before 1289 are not dated). Cliopatria's 1188 step (5.96 k to 3.2 k km2) is not explained by any page opened. The Tripoli page does not mention Hattin, Jubail, Arqa, Margat, Safita or Akkar. The 1271 loss region is the difference of two Cliopatria shapes, not a page-named list. Union with Antioch: Bohemond IV (count from 1189) took Antioch in 1201 and Bohemonds V and VI held both, a personal union with no border change (the County of Tripoli page; the War of the Antiochene Succession page notes that he "could not hold both at once" with limited resources). Vassalage: the infobox lists the county as a vassal of Jerusalem, Antioch and the Mongol Empire without years; the Kingdom of Jerusalem dossier carries Jerusalem's lordship 1109-1289 (Bertrand "the south as Baldwin's vassal"). The Mongol and Antioch relations need the suzerains' dossiers. Counterparts needing dossiers: banu-ammar (the emirate of Tripoli before 1109, no Cliopatria row); the Hospitallers and the Genoese quarter are not territory in this dossier. Gazetteer names needed: Batroun, Nephin (Enfeh), Montferrand (Ba'rin); coordinates are used for Batroun and Nephin. Tripoli is written {"place": "Tripoli", "country": "Lebanon"}.
